subject.title: Add accessibility config option to disable emojis and unicode symbols in TUI

question: Which supported terminal accessibility contract should OpenClaw adopt: a plain-text mode with named ASCII replacements, a narrower emoji-only opt-out, or a broader accessibility design that first includes the pi-tui selection indicator?
rationale: The repository needs a stable user-facing configuration key and replacement vocabulary before changing multiple TUI surfaces; the closed prior proposal does not establish that product contract.

options.title: Adopt a full plain-text TUI mode
options.body: Add one documented UI accessibility setting with consistent ASCII replacements across OpenClaw-owned rendering, while tracking any missing pi-tui control seam separately.

options.title: Start with OpenClaw-owned symbols only
options.body: Remove or replace emoji and decorative separators owned by OpenClaw now, leaving the pi-tui selection indicator unchanged until upstream support exists.

options.title: Defer pending broader accessibility design
options.body: Keep the issue open while maintainers define a broader terminal accessibility approach and test criteria with affected users.

recommendation.title: Adopt a full plain-text TUI mode
recommendation.body: Add one documented UI accessibility setting with consistent ASCII replacements across OpenClaw-owned rendering, while tracking any missing pi-tui control seam separately.

likelyOwner.reason: The central TUI and tool-display architecture has strong feature-history ownership evidence for this product and implementation decision.
